newsitem.title: CANADA: CanOxy sees higher cash flow from Wascana.
newsitem.headline: CanOxy sees higher cash flow from Wascana.

text.p: Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd expected its cash flow to increase and earnings to fall after the first partial year with Wascana Energy Inc under its corporate umbrella, CanOxy chief executive David Hentschel said on Tuesday.
Hentschel told a conference call he expected CanOxy's cash flow per share to rise about C$1.20 above previous forecasts for 1997 to C$6.55 if the C$2 billion deal went through.
He said earnings would likely drop about C$0.50 a share from where they would have been without the acquisition, but were expected to growing in 1998 and beyond.
CanOxy emerged on Tuesday as a white knight for Wascana, offering C$20.50 cash per Wascana share.
The offer, which has the blessing of both firms' boards of directors, eclipsed a C$1.7 billion cash and stock bid from Talisman Energy Inc.
"Not only is this a great operational fit, but this deal puts the excess cash flow being generated by CanOxy to excellent use funding low-risk steady growth," Hentschel said.
He said the firm would have debt of about C$2.5 billion after the deal, including its own C$400 million, Wascana's C$245 million and financing for the purchase.

Hentschel said CanOxy, which bought under 10 percent of Wascana's shares starting in December, opted to offer cash because its shares traded at a lower cash flow multiple than Talisman's. He attributed that to most of its operations, including a high number of high-risk exploration plays, being located outside Canada.
Also, CanOxy had not issued stock since 1983 and wanted to protect its shareholders from dilution, he said.

He said CanOxy would produce about 264,000 barrels oil equivalent per day worldwide, including 115,000 in Canada, after the deal, giving the firm a better balance between Canadian and international operations.
Hentschel said the price of its offer gave no value to Wascana's own international operations, which include exploration and production in Algeria and Venezuela.
The company would be buying Wascana at a price of C$7 per barrel of oil equivalent of proven reserves and C$6.10 per barrel of proven plus half-probable reserves, he said.
The median Canadian proven plus half-probable reserve price for several recent deals was C$6.17 per barrel.

Hentschel said CanOxy executives were slated to begin a roadshow to sell the deal to investors. Meetings were to start in Toronto on Wednesday and continue in New York and Boston on Thursday and Montreal on Friday.
